column1: # Hand-authored territory and footprint spec for entries Glottolog or
# Glottography leaves short. Most rows are entries with no language-area
# polygon. A few have a polygon but no country data, and are here so the
# overlap report can still see where they are.
# Adding an entry here is the decision that it gets an admin boundary instead of
# a language area. Run pipeline.coverage first; it prints exactly who needs a row.
# territory: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or ISO 3166-2 where a country subdivision is the
# real footprint. Space-separated, most important first. These are also what
# pipeline.overlaps uses to find entries that must not share a session.
# boundary: admin-0 (Natural Earth countries), admin-1 (Natural Earth states and
# provinces) or gisco (Eurostat NUTS, which has the Spanish communities).
# These four have language-area polygons already. They are here only because
# Glottolog's country list for them is "GB", which cannot tell Scotland from
# Wales and made the overlap report collide every British entry with every other.#
# selector: how to cut the polygon out of Natural Earth, as key=value pairs
# matched against feature properties, with | meaning or. admin0 is
# ne_50m_admin_0_countries, admin1 is ne_10m_admin_1_states_provinces, which is
# province level, so regions are selected by its region or gu_a3 fields rather
# than by an ISO subdivision code. Empty selector means Glottography already
# draws this entry and the row exists only to give the overlap report a
# territory Glottolog left blank or too coarse.

column6: The official-languages outline added Somalia, Djibouti, Comoros, Eritrea and Chad, where Arabic is official but not the mother tongue. This is the belt where it is.
Northern Aragon, mainly Huesca. The southern half of the community is Spanish-speaking, so weight the north.
The entry resolves to Eastern Armenian. Bouckaert had a second blob near Istanbul, which is Western Armenian territory and historical at that.
Asturias. Glottolog has no country data for this node at all, being a dialect of Asturian-Leonese-Cantabrian.
Australia. Population-weighted hard, since the interior is empty.
The entry resolves to North Azerbaijani, the republic. DiACL's polygon also covered Iranian Azerbaijan, which is South Azerbaijani and a different entry.
Croatian is co-official in Bosnia, so the official-languages outline covered it too. Croatia is where a player should pin.
Galicia. Fringes of Asturias, Leon, Zamora and Extremadura are also Galician-speaking and can be added as lower-weight polygons.
Ghana.
Hong Kong. The one English dialect node Glottolog gives its own coordinate.
India. Urban-weighted, since Indian English is a city and education variety rather than an evenly spread one.
Rests on the official-languages outline, and for a national language the national outline is the speech area. Checked by eye, it is the archipelago.
Ireland. The living Gaeltacht is the western fringe, which the polygon carries and this row does not.

The Britain and Ireland atlas draws this one directly, so the polygon exists. Territory is recorded here only so pipeline.overlaps can see it, since Glottolog gives the node no country data. The atlas is historical, so eyeball the shape before using it.
Jamaica.
Kenya.
Malaysia.
New Zealand.
Nigeria.
United States and Canada. The largest footprint in the pool, so population weighting is doing all the work here.
DiACL, but checked by eye: North and South Ossetia, which is right for Iron Ossetian.
Philippines.
The entry resolves to Cusco Quechua, not Quechuan as a family. DiACL drew the whole Andean spine from Ecuador to Bolivia, which is every Quechuan variety at once.
DiACL, but checked by eye: the Logudorese area of central and northern Sardinia, which matches the variety the entry resolves to.
Scotland. Carries local id stan1293-scotland, see data/local-ids.tsv.
Hebrides and the western Highlands, not all of Scotland. The polygon is the real shape, this row is only for territory comparison.
Serbia and Montenegro. Republika Srpska is genuinely Serbian-speaking but admin-0 Bosnia would take the Federation with it, so it is left out until there is a sub-national cut.
Singapore. Tiny footprint, so almost any pin in Southeast Asia scores on distance rather than containment.

Southeast England including London. Cut from NUTS-1 UKI (London), UKJ (South East) and UKH (East of England) rather than all of England. The ISO code here is GB-ENG only so the overlap report can compare it against Scotland and Wales, which it correctly does not touch.
South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, weighted toward South Africa. Glottolog's node covers all three.

Wales. Glottolog also lists AR for the Patagonian settlement at Y Wladfa, a few hundred speakers, left out here so it does not collide with South American entries. Add it as a very low weight polygon if wanted.
Wales. Distinct from Welsh itself, which concentrates in the north and west.

DiACL draws the pre-war heartland in eastern Poland, which is not where Yiddish is spoken now. Today it is Haredi communities: New York, Jerusalem, Tel Aviv with Bnei Brak, and Antwerp. London and Montreal are the next two to add.
